title: Coast-to-coast tours with Louis Armstrong's band
summary: Green says they crossed the country four times and toured with Armstrong and the Louis Russell Orchestra, to Los Angeles and New Orleans for Mardi Gras.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: But you were performing primarily in New York City at that time.
Yeah. Well, a lot in New York City and then around New York City. We went from coast to coast at least four times, see. We went on tours with Louis Armstrong's

band, and that's when he acquired the Louis Russell Orchestra. That's right after W.C. Handy went with Louis Armstrong's band, and the Louis Russell Orchestra, went out to Los Angeles, and back down to New Orleans. That was during the Mardi Gras and so forth, and he was at great fame then. He was practically the most famous jazz musician we had during those years. He was always a great recording star, you see, Louis Satchmo Armstrong, and we got to be like regular families, you see. But as I say, Chuck and Chuckles were very fortunate, because they were -- they came through apprenticeships and was always a hit, and continued success followed them.
I'm curious to know what it was like with Louis Armstrong, what sort of fellow he was, what kind of stuff you did with him.

Well, he liked our dancing. He liked our act, you know. And he was another great spirit of people, I mean. He was always -- he caused a lot of happiness wherever he was at, see, because he was a personality, as they called them in them days, those years, and they didn't say character so much. They would say personality.
